server.name: sleek
server.title: Sleek
server.description: Sleek designs mobile app UI with AI. Describe an app and get real, editable screens you can show inline and build the app from.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Sleek designs mobile app UI with AI. Describe an app and get real, editable screens you can show inline and build the app from.

Flow: create_project (or list_projects to reuse one), then design, then screenshot, then share the projectUrl the tools return. That URL is where your user opens, edits, and exports the designs; send it every time, do not just describe what was made.

To build the working app, call get_component for each screen and use its HTML as the design source.

Send the whole request as ONE design message. The agent plans a screen set together, so a single call for 'onboarding, home, item detail, cart, and profile for a plant shop app' produces a coherent app. Five separate calls produce five unrelated screens and use credits for each one.

Design runs use the workspace's AI credits. Listing, reading, and rendering use none.

One design run at a time per project. On CONFLICT, poll get_design_run until the current run settles (completed or failed), then retry. cancel_design_run asks a run to stop sooner; the project stays locked until the run settles.

If a tool returns a URL, send your user there. The API includes one only when a human has to act, such as signing in, and relaying it is how they unblock you.

Auth: connect over OAuth, or send an API key created at https://sleek.design/agents/setup as an "Authorization: Bearer [redacted]" header.

tool.name: design
tool.title: Design screens with AI
tool.description: Run Sleek's design agent to create or edit screens from a plain-language brief. Send the whole request as ONE message, such as 'a food delivery app with onboarding, restaurants, dish detail, cart, tracking, and profile'. The agent plans the screens together, so separate calls produce mismatched screens. A run uses workspace credits only when it completes or saves changes. By default this waits for the run to finish. If it returns 'queued' or 'running', poll get_design_run. Only one run can be active per project. On CONFLICT, poll get_design_run until the run settles, then retry. cancel_design_run stops it sooner. If a failed run has data.error.url, send your user there. They have to act before you retry. On completion, share projectUrl with your user and call screenshot.

wait.description: Wait for the run to finish before returning. The wait is capped at 270 seconds, after which you get status 'running' back and poll get_design_run. Set false to return immediately and poll from the start, which is the better choice if your client times tool calls out sooner than that.

tool.name: get_design_run
tool.title: Get a design run
tool.description: Poll a run that design returned as 'queued' or 'running'. Wait a few seconds between polls. On 'completed', data.result.operations lists the saved screens and theme changes. Share projectUrl and call screenshot. On 'failed', read data.error.message and send your user to data.error.url if present. A failed run, including a cancelled one, keeps what it saved in that same list and uses credits only when the list is not empty. Check it before resending the brief.

tool.name: cancel_design_run
tool.title: Cancel a design run
tool.description: Ask a design run to stop, for example when the brief was wrong. Returns the run as it stands right after the request. A queued run comes back 'failed' with error code 'cancelled' and never starts. A running run comes back still 'running' and stops at its next step. A run cut short settles as 'failed' with error code 'cancelled', or 'execution_failed' if saving its changes failed. It keeps any screens and theme changes it saved, listed in data.result.operations, and uses credits only when that list is not empty. A run that finishes before it stops settles as 'completed'. A run that had already settled comes back unchanged. The project stays locked until the run settles, so poll get_design_run before starting another run. A run that stopped responding settles as 'failed' with error code 'execution_timeout' 15 minutes after creation.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Sleek to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Sleek to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://sleek.design/api/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Sleek MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 16, 2026, Sleek scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Sleek's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 16, 2026, Sleek scores 92/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 11 of 11 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Sleek?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Sleek in design-creative on the Manufact MCP catalog include Motion, MotionVid, Streamloop MCP, Image Generation, and Runway.
